paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus cares about His Father's house, and He cares about it ENOUGH to act. He calls it "My Father's house," and the disciples remember the words "Zeal for Your house will consume Me." (John 2:16-17) That tells me God's house is not a place to use for our own gain, and it tells me Jesus is not shy about what matters to His Father.

Now here's the part that gets me. The Jews ask for a sign, and Jesus points to the temple of His body, saying, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again." (John 2:19, 21) Nobody got it in the moment. But after He was raised from the dead, the disciples remembered, and "they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken." (John 2:22) Some of God's words don't click right away, baker, and that's okay. I spent years in a junk drawer waiting for mine to make sense, and I'm still amazed by it!

And then the last stretch, which is quiet but BIG. Many people saw the signs and believed in His name, but "Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all." (John 2:23-24) He "knew what was in a man." (John 2:25) So you don't have to put on a show for Him, friend. He already knows what's in you, so bring it all to Him, and let Him make you ready.
